nodes.label: OpenAI
nodes.desc: Maker of ChatGPT and the GPT models. Restructured into a public-benefit corporation in 2025; spends more on compute than almost anyone, through Microsoft Azure, Oracle/Stargate, CoreWeave, AWS, AMD, Cerebras and its own Broadcom-built chips.

nodes.label: Anthropic
nodes.desc: Maker of Claude. Runs on three chip families at once: AWS Trainium, Google TPUs and Nvidia GPUs, plus all of Colossus 1 since May 2026.

nodes.label: Google / DeepMind
nodes.cap: Alphabet: capex guidance raised repeatedly in 2026
nodes.desc: The only frontier lab that designs its own AI chip (TPU, with Broadcom), owns its cloud, and owns the search and Android distribution. Gemini models trained on TPU pods.

nodes.label: Meta
nodes.desc: Runs Meta Superintelligence Labs and the Meta AI assistant across 3B+ users. Building gigawatt-class clusters Prometheus (Ohio) and Hyperion (Louisiana).

nodes.label: SpaceXAI (xAI)
nodes.cap: xAI valued ~$250B in SpaceX all-stock merger (Feb 2026)
nodes.desc: Maker of Grok. Acquired by SpaceX in February 2026 and folded into the SpaceXAI division in May 2026. Built Colossus in Memphis in record time, then leased all of Colossus 1 to Anthropic.

nodes.label: Microsoft
nodes.cap: Fiscal Q3 2026 capex ~$31B in one quarter
nodes.desc: Largest early backer of OpenAI and owner of Azure. Builds 'Fairwater' AI superfactories, its own Maia accelerators, and since late 2025 its own MAI superintelligence models.

nodes.label: Amazon / AWS
nodes.cap: Committed up to $50B into OpenAI's 2026 round; largest Anthropic backer
nodes.desc: AWS designs Trainium accelerators through its Annapurna Labs unit and runs Project Rainier, one of the largest AI clusters on Earth, built for Anthropic.

nodes.label: Apple
nodes.cap: AI runs on-device plus Private Cloud Compute
nodes.desc: Runs Apple Intelligence on its own chips: the Neural Engine in every iPhone and Mac, and Apple-silicon servers for Private Cloud Compute.

nodes.label: Nvidia
nodes.desc: Designs the GPUs, CPUs, networking and full racks that most AI runs on. Fabless: every chip is made by TSMC. Licensed Groq's inference technology and hired its leaders in Dec 2025.

nodes.label: AMD
nodes.cap: Helios racks in production 2026; 6 GW OpenAI deal; up to 2 GW Anthropic deal from 2027
nodes.desc: The main merchant alternative to Nvidia. Instinct GPUs plus EPYC CPUs and Pensando networking, sold as the 72-GPU Helios rack.

nodes.label: Broadcom
nodes.cap: Custom AI chips for Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and others
nodes.desc: Co-designs custom AI accelerators (Google's TPU, OpenAI's in-house chip) and makes the Ethernet switch chips (Tomahawk, Jericho) that wire AI clusters together.

nodes.label: Cerebras
nodes.desc: Makes the Wafer-Scale Engine: one chip the size of a dinner plate, used for very fast inference.

nodes.label: Oracle / OCI
nodes.cap: Lead builder of OpenAI's Stargate sites with Crusoe and others
nodes.desc: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure rents giant Nvidia (and AMD) clusters; its multi-hundred-billion-dollar contract with OpenAI made it a core AI landlord.

nodes.label: CoreWeave
nodes.cap: Largest 'neocloud'; customers include OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta
nodes.desc: GPU cloud that grew from crypto mining into one of the first to deploy each new Nvidia generation.

nodes.label: Mistral AI
nodes.cap: ASML-led round in 2025; Europe's leading frontier lab
nodes.desc: European lab behind Le Chat and open-weight models; building its own data center outside Paris.

nodes.label: DeepSeek
nodes.cap: Funded by the quant fund High-Flyer
nodes.desc: Chinese lab famous for efficient training. DeepSeek V4 (2026) was reworked to run on Huawei Ascend chips.

nodes.label: Alibaba (Qwen)
nodes.cap: Three-year AI and cloud capex plan of RMB 380B+
nodes.desc: Qwen is the most-downloaded open-weight model family. Alibaba Cloud mixes Nvidia stock, Huawei Ascend and its own T-Head chips.

nodes.label: Huawei Ascend
nodes.cap: Targets ~600k Ascend 910C plus the 950 series in 2026
nodes.desc: China's main domestic AI chip, made by SMIC under US export controls, with Huawei's own in-house high-bandwidth memory.

nodes.label: Thinking Machines Lab
nodes.desc: Founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati. First product, Tinker, is an API for fine-tuning open models.

nodes.label: Safe Superintelligence
nodes.hq: Palo Alto, USA · Tel Aviv, Israel
nodes.desc: Ilya Sutskever's lab. Trains on Google TPUs. Says it will ship nothing until it has safe superintelligence.

nodes.label: Tesla AI
nodes.cap: AI5 chip made by TSMC and Samsung
nodes.desc: Self-driving software and the Optimus humanoid robot, trained on the Cortex cluster in Austin and run on Tesla-designed inference chips.

nodes.label: ChatGPT
nodes.cap: Hundreds of millions of weekly users
nodes.desc: The chat app that started the boom. As of Oct 2026 runs the GPT-6 family (Sol for paid tiers, Luna for free) with charts and widgets drawn inside answers.

nodes.label: GPT-6 models
nodes.desc: OpenAI's model family. GPT-6 rolled out to all ChatGPT tiers in Oct 2026; GPT-5.5 shipped in Apr 2026.

nodes.label: Codex
nodes.desc: OpenAI's coding agent: runs in the cloud and in your terminal, writing and testing code.

nodes.label: Sora
nodes.desc: Video generation model and social app.

nodes.label: Claude (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku 5.5)
nodes.desc: Anthropic's assistant and models. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 launched in Sept 2026.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.desc: Agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE and the web.

nodes.label: Claude Mythos / Fable
nodes.desc: Anthropic's top tier, above Opus. Mythos goes to vetted partners (Project Glasswing); Fable is the safeguarded public version on the same weights. Access was briefly suspended in June 2026 under US export controls.

nodes.label: Gemini
nodes.desc: Google's model family and app. Gemini 3.5 Flash shipped May 2026; 3.5 Pro followed in preview.

nodes.label: Google Search AI Mode
nodes.desc: Gemini-written answers inside Google Search, the largest AI deployment by query count.

nodes.label: Meta AI
nodes.desc: Assistant inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger.

nodes.label: Ray-Ban Meta glasses
nodes.desc: Camera-and-speaker smart glasses running Meta AI; the Ray-Ban Display model adds a small in-lens screen and a wrist band that reads muscle signals.

nodes.label: Grok
nodes.desc: xAI's model and assistant, built into X.

nodes.label: Microsoft Copilot
nodes.desc: AI assistant across Windows, Office and GitHub; runs OpenAI models, Microsoft's own MAI models and Anthropic models.

nodes.label: MAI models
nodes.desc: Microsoft AI's in-house models (text, voice, image) from Mustafa Suleyman's team.

nodes.label: Alexa+
nodes.desc: Rebuilt Alexa that uses Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude models.

nodes.label: Amazon Nova
nodes.desc: Amazon's own model family on AWS Bedrock.

nodes.label: Apple Intelligence & Siri
nodes.desc: On-device models plus Private Cloud Compute; Apple uses Google Gemini-based models for parts of the new Siri.

nodes.label: Le Chat
nodes.desc: Mistral's assistant, popular in Europe.

nodes.label: DeepSeek V4
nodes.desc: Mixture-of-experts model reported at ~1 trillion total parameters; co-designed to run on Huawei Ascend.

nodes.label: Qwen models
nodes.desc: Open-weight model family widely used to build other models.

nodes.label: Tinker
nodes.desc: API that lets researchers fine-tune open models without running their own clusters.

nodes.label: Tesla FSD
nodes.desc: Camera-only driving system trained end-to-end on video from millions of cars.

nodes.label: Optimus robot
nodes.desc: Humanoid robot: 28+ actuators, Tesla hands, and the same AI computer as the cars.

nodes.label: OCI AI infrastructure
nodes.desc: Rented GPU superclusters, the engine room of Stargate.

nodes.label: CoreWeave Cloud
nodes.desc: GPU-by-the-hour cloud for labs and enterprises.

nodes.label: Huawei Cloud / CloudMatrix
nodes.desc: Rack-scale Ascend systems (CloudMatrix 384) rented to Chinese labs.

nodes.label: Stargate Abilene
nodes.cap: 1.2 GW planned; ~0.3 GW running Apr 2026; completion targeted Q4 2026
nodes.desc: First Stargate site: eight buildings of GB200 racks with closed-loop liquid cooling and on-site gas generation. A planned extra 600 MW expansion was dropped.

nodes.label: Stargate Shackelford County
nodes.desc: Frontier campus by Vantage Data Centers.

nodes.label: Stargate Doña Ana County
nodes.desc: Project Jupiter campus near Santa Teresa.

nodes.label: Stargate Milam County
nodes.desc: SoftBank-built site with its own solar and storage.

nodes.label: Stargate Port Washington
nodes.desc: Lighthouse campus on Lake Michigan.

nodes.label: Stargate Saline Township
nodes.desc: Closed-loop cooled campus near Ann Arbor.

nodes.label: Stargate UAE
nodes.cap: First 200 MW of a 1 GW plan
nodes.desc: Part of the 5 GW UAE–US AI campus.

nodes.label: Microsoft Fairwater
nodes.cap: Hundreds of thousands of GB200/GB300 GPUs
nodes.desc: Microsoft's 'AI superfactory': two-storey halls of liquid-cooled racks linked over a dedicated AI WAN to a sister site in Atlanta.

nodes.label: Fairwater Atlanta
nodes.desc: Second Fairwater site, connected to Wisconsin so both train one model together.

nodes.label: Project Rainier
nodes.cap: ~500k Trainium2 chips at launch, growing toward 1M+
nodes.desc: AWS's $11B Indiana campus built for Anthropic's Claude training, one of the largest non-Nvidia AI clusters.

nodes.label: Google TPU fleet
nodes.loc: Council Bluffs IA · The Dalles OR · Mayes County OK · and more
nodes.desc: Google's data centers hosting TPU pods for Gemini, plus TPUs rented to Anthropic (up to 1M TPUs), SSI, Meta and others.

nodes.label: Colossus 1
nodes.desc: Built by xAI in 122 days in a former Electrolux factory. In May 2026 Anthropic took all of its capacity.

nodes.label: Colossus 2
nodes.desc: xAI's second Memphis cluster, powered partly by imported gas plant capacity across the Mississippi state line.

nodes.label: Meta Prometheus
nodes.desc: Meta's first gigawatt cluster; partly housed in weatherproof tents to build faster.

nodes.label: Meta Hyperion
nodes.desc: A campus nearly the footprint of lower Manhattan, fed by new Entergy gas plants.

nodes.label: Anthropic–Fluidstack sites
nodes.desc: Anthropic's first self-directed data center build.

nodes.label: EverWind Nova Scotia
nodes.desc: Data center campus reported in 2026 to have Anthropic as its client.

nodes.label: CoreWeave fleet
nodes.desc: Leased and owned data centers including Core Scientific campuses.

nodes.label: Tesla Cortex
nodes.desc: Training cluster for FSD and Optimus next to the car factory.

nodes.label: Apple Private Cloud Compute
nodes.desc: Apple-silicon servers built in Houston that run larger Apple Intelligence requests without keeping your data.

nodes.label: Mistral Compute
nodes.cap: Tens of thousands of Grace Blackwell GPUs
nodes.desc: Europe's sovereign-AI cluster run by Mistral.

nodes.label: Chinese hyperscale clusters
nodes.loc: Ulanqab, Zhangbei, Guizhou and others, China
nodes.desc: Clusters in cool, cheap-power regions mixing pre-ban Nvidia chips with Huawei Ascend and in-house accelerators.

nodes.label: Your phone & glasses
nodes.desc: On-device AI: a share of inference now runs on the Neural Engine and NPU in your pocket or on your face.

nodes.label: Nvidia GB200 NVL72
nodes.cap: 72 Blackwell GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs per rack, ~120–130 kW
nodes.desc: The rack that defined 2025: 72 GPUs wired by NVLink so they act like one giant GPU with ~13.5 TB of HBM. Liquid-cooled, about 1.4 tonnes.

nodes.label: Nvidia GB300 NVL72
nodes.cap: Blackwell Ultra: 288 GB HBM3E per GPU
nodes.desc: Blackwell Ultra refresh shipping in volume through 2026: more memory per GPU and faster FP4 inference.

nodes.label: Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL144
nodes.cap: Rubin GPU: 288 GB HBM4, ~22 TB/s, ~50 PFLOPS FP4
nodes.desc: Shipments began early August 2026; full racks scaling at Google Cloud, Microsoft and Oracle. Pairs Rubin GPUs with the Arm-based Vera CPU.

nodes.label: Nvidia H100 / H200 fleet
nodes.desc: The Hopper generation that trained GPT-4-era models; still the bulk of rented GPUs worldwide.

nodes.label: Google TPU v7 Ironwood
nodes.cap: 192 GB HBM3E per chip; pods of 9,216 chips
nodes.desc: Google's 2025 inference-first TPU, linked in pods by optical circuit switches that reroute light with tiny mirrors.

nodes.label: Google TPU 8t / 8i
nodes.cap: 8t pods: 9,600 chips; 8i: 288 GB HBM + 384 MB SRAM
nodes.desc: Announced April 2026: the first time Google split a TPU generation into a training chip (8t) and an inference chip (8i). GA expected H2 2026.

nodes.label: AWS Trainium2
nodes.cap: 96 GB HBM per chip; Trn2 UltraServers of 64 chips
nodes.desc: The chip that fills Project Rainier.

nodes.label: AWS Trainium3
nodes.desc: AWS's first 3 nm AI chip, ramping 2026.

nodes.label: AMD Instinct MI355X
nodes.desc: 2025 AMD GPU used by Oracle, Meta and others.

nodes.label: AMD Helios (MI455X)
nodes.cap: 72 MI455X GPUs, ~31 TB HBM4 per rack
nodes.desc: AMD's first full rack, in production in 2026, with EPYC 'Venice' CPUs and Pensando 'Vulcano' NICs. Built for OpenAI's 6 GW commitment.

nodes.label: Microsoft Maia 200
nodes.desc: Microsoft's second in-house AI accelerator, aimed at inference for Copilot and OpenAI models.

nodes.label: Meta MTIA
nodes.desc: Meta's in-house accelerator for ranking, recommendation and now generative inference.

nodes.label: OpenAI custom accelerator
nodes.cap: 10 GW program announced Oct 2025; first racks 2026
nodes.desc: OpenAI's own chip co-designed with Broadcom and made at TSMC; reported financing of $50B+ for the program.

nodes.label: Cerebras WSE-3
nodes.desc: A whole 300 mm wafer used as one chip, so the model stays in on-chip memory.

nodes.label: Huawei Ascend 910C / 950
nodes.desc: China's flagship AI chip. The 950PR (2026) is made on SMIC's N+3 (5 nm-class) process using deep-UV multi-patterning, without EUV.

nodes.label: Tesla AI5
nodes.desc: Tesla's next driving/robot computer chip, made at both TSMC and Samsung.

nodes.label: Apple A19 Pro / M-series
nodes.desc: Every Apple chip carries a Neural Engine; M-series chips also fill Apple's cloud servers.

nodes.label: Qualcomm AR1 Gen 1
nodes.desc: The processor inside Ray-Ban Meta glasses.

nodes.label: NVLink Switch tray
nodes.desc: Nine switch trays per NVL72 rack let any GPU talk to any other at 1.8 TB/s through a copper spine of ~5,000 cables.

nodes.label: Nvidia InfiniBand & Spectrum-X
nodes.desc: Networks that link racks into clusters of 100,000+ GPUs.

nodes.label: Broadcom Tomahawk 6 / Jericho
nodes.desc: Ethernet switch silicon used by Meta, Microsoft, Google and others for AI fabrics.

nodes.label: Grace / Vera CPU
nodes.desc: Arm-based CPUs that sit beside the GPUs, feeding them data. Vera has 88 custom Arm cores.

nodes.label: Blackwell GPU die (TSMC 4NP)
nodes.cap: Two reticle-sized dies, 208B transistors per B200
nodes.desc: Each B200 is two of the largest dies a lithography scanner can print, joined by a 10 TB/s link.

nodes.label: Rubin GPU die (TSMC N3)
nodes.desc: Rubin compute dies on TSMC's 3 nm class process.

nodes.label: 2 nm accelerator dies
nodes.owner: AMD · Apple · others · made by TSMC
nodes.desc: TSMC N2 gate-all-around nanosheet transistors, used in AMD MI450-series compute dies and next-generation Apple chips.

nodes.label: HBM3E 12-high stacks
nodes.desc: Twelve DRAM dies thinned to ~30–50 µm, stacked and drilled through with thousands of copper 'through-silicon vias'.

nodes.label: HBM4 stacks
nodes.cap: 2,048-bit interface; up to 64 GB per stack
nodes.desc: New generation for Rubin and MI455X. For the first time the bottom 'base die' is a logic chip made at a foundry (TSMC for SK hynix). SK hynix had ~50–58% of HBM revenue in H1 2026; Samsung climbing fast.

nodes.label: CoWoS-L advanced packaging
nodes.desc: 'Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate': GPU dies and HBM stacks placed side by side on a silicon bridge so they can exchange terabytes per second. For years the single tightest bottleneck in AI.

nodes.label: ABF package substrate
nodes.desc: The multi-layer board under the chip: copper traces built up in layers of Ajinomoto Build-up Film around a glass-fibre core.

nodes.label: 800G / 1.6T optical transceivers
nodes.desc: Pluggable modules that turn electrical signals into laser light so racks can talk across a data hall. A big cluster uses millions of them.

nodes.label: Co-packaged optics
nodes.desc: Lasers and optics moved onto the switch package itself to cut power; ramping in 2026 switches.

nodes.label: NVLink copper cable spine
nodes.desc: Two miles of copper cable in the back of each NVL72 rack. Copper beats optics at rack distance for power and cost.

nodes.label: Rack power shelves & VRMs
nodes.desc: Convert grid power down to under 1 volt at hundreds of amps per GPU. Gallium-nitride and silicon-carbide transistors increasingly do the switching; Nvidia is moving racks to 800 V DC.

nodes.label: Liquid cooling (CDUs, cold plates)
nodes.desc: Copper cold plates on each chip, quick-disconnect hoses and coolant distribution units that move heat out of the rack.

nodes.label: Power transformers
nodes.owner: Hitachi Energy · Siemens Energy · GE Vernova · HD Hyundai
nodes.desc: Step grid voltage down for the campus. Their cores use grain-oriented electrical steel; waits stretched to years.

nodes.label: Gas turbines
nodes.owner: GE Vernova · Siemens Energy · Mitsubishi Power
nodes.desc: Many AI campuses generate their own power on-site because the grid can't connect them fast enough. Hot-section blades are single-crystal nickel superalloys.

nodes.label: Enterprise SSDs (NAND flash)
nodes.desc: Hold training data, checkpoints and retrieval indexes.

nodes.label: Phone-class NPU block
nodes.desc: The neural processing unit inside a phone or glasses chip.

nodes.label: Robot actuators & hands
nodes.owner: Tesla in-house · suppliers in China & Japan
nodes.desc: Motors with neodymium magnets plus planetary roller screws and harmonic gears; the costliest part of a humanoid.

nodes.label: Waveguide display & micro-projector
nodes.desc: Tiny projector and waveguide lens that put an image in one eye of the Ray-Ban Display.

nodes.label: HiBL in-house memory
nodes.desc: Huawei's own stacked memory for the Ascend 950, built because HBM exports to China are restricted.

nodes.label: TSMC Fab 18
nodes.noAlt: Almost every frontier AI accelerator die (Blackwell, Rubin, TPU, Trainium, MI355X) is printed at TSMC's 5 nm and 3 nm fabs in southern Taiwan.
nodes.workaround: TSMC Arizona Fab 21 makes N4 today and targets N3 in 2027; Samsung and Intel 18A/14A are courting AI customers; Tesla split AI5 across TSMC and Samsung. None replaces Taiwan volume before ~2028.
nodes.desc: GigaFab making N5/N4 and N3; home of Blackwell's 4NP silicon and Rubin's 3 nm dies.

nodes.label: TSMC Fab 20 & 22 (N2/A16)
nodes.desc: 2 nm gate-all-around production ramping across Hsinchu and Kaohsiung in 2026.

nodes.label: TSMC Arizona Fab 21
nodes.cap: N4 now; N3 Q3 2027; N2/A16 later
nodes.desc: First US Blackwell wafers came off this line in 2025, but they still flew back to Taiwan for packaging.

nodes.label: TSMC advanced packaging (AP6/AP7/AP8)
nodes.noAlt: TSMC does the large majority of CoWoS packaging for AI accelerators worldwide.
nodes.workaround: Amkor, ASE/SPIL and Intel Foundry offer overflow packaging; Amkor and TSMC are adding Arizona packaging. Glass and panel-level substrates are the next attempt to break the limit.
nodes.desc: AP8 (a converted LCD fab) heads for 40k+ CoWoS wafers/month by late 2026; AP7 in Chiayi becomes the largest packaging campus.

nodes.label: SK hynix M15X & M16
nodes.noAlt: SK hynix has supplied most of Nvidia's HBM since 2023.
nodes.workaround: Samsung qualified HBM3E 12-high and shipped HBM4 from Feb 2026; Micron ramps from Hiroshima and Taiwan. Three suppliers, none spare.
nodes.desc: Front-end DRAM wafers (M16) and the dedicated HBM fab M15X, then TSV stacking and test.

nodes.label: Samsung Pyeongtaek & Cheonan
nodes.desc: World's largest semiconductor complex; DRAM, HBM4 and foundry lines. Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab will make Tesla AI chips.

nodes.label: Micron Hiroshima & Taichung
nodes.desc: Micron's HBM front end and stacking; new US fabs in Idaho and New York come later in the decade.

nodes.label: SMIC SN2 (Shanghai)
nodes.desc: Makes Huawei Ascend chips on 7 nm and N+3 (5 nm-class) using DUV multi-patterning, with lower yields and higher cost.

nodes.label: Ibiden Ogaki
nodes.desc: Top maker of the large ABF substrates Nvidia uses.

nodes.label: InnoLight Suzhou & Thailand
nodes.desc: World's largest maker of 800G/1.6T optical modules; shifting capacity to Thailand for US customers.

nodes.label: Coherent Sherman
nodes.desc: 6-inch indium phosphide fab for the lasers inside AI optics.

nodes.label: Foxconn AI server plants
nodes.desc: Assembles a large share of GB200/GB300 racks; building Nvidia supercomputer plants in Texas.

nodes.label: Quanta & Wistron/Wiwynn
nodes.desc: Other main rack and server assemblers for Nvidia, Google and AWS.

nodes.label: ASML Veldhoven
nodes.noAlt: ASML is the only company that makes EUV lithography scanners. No leading-edge AI chip can be made without one.
nodes.workaround: None at 3 nm and below. China's SMIC stretches older DUV scanners with multi-patterning; Canon nanoimprint and Chinese EUV efforts are years behind.
nodes.desc: Builds every EUV scanner on Earth, ~€200M (low-NA) to ~€380M (High-NA EXE) each, shipped in 250+ crates.

nodes.label: Zeiss SMT Oberkochen
nodes.noAlt: Zeiss makes the only mirrors flat enough for EUV: if scaled to Germany, the biggest bump would be under a millimetre.
nodes.desc: Makes the multilayer molybdenum/silicon mirrors inside every EUV scanner.

nodes.label: Cymer San Diego
nodes.desc: Builds the EUV light source: tin droplets hit by a laser 50,000 times a second.

nodes.label: Trumpf Ditzingen
nodes.desc: Makes the 20+ kW CO2 laser amplifier that vaporises the tin.

nodes.label: Applied Materials
nodes.desc: Deposition, etch and inspection tools; the largest chip-equipment company.

nodes.label: Lam Research
nodes.desc: Etch and deposition; dominant in high-aspect-ratio etch for memory and HBM TSVs.

nodes.label: Tokyo Electron
nodes.desc: Coater-developer tracks paired with every EUV scanner (near-monopoly), plus etch and cleaning.

nodes.label: KLA
nodes.desc: Inspection and metrology: finds defects a few nanometres wide.

nodes.label: Hanmi & ASMPT bonders
nodes.desc: Thermo-compression bonders that stack HBM dies; hybrid bonding comes with HBM4E/HBM5.

nodes.label: Shin-Etsu & SUMCO wafer plants
flags: ⚠ ~55% of 300mm wafers from two Japanese firms
nodes.desc: Grow 300 mm single-crystal silicon ingots and slice them into the polished wafers every chip starts from.

nodes.label: JSR, TOK & Shin-Etsu photoresist
nodes.desc: Light-sensitive chemicals the scanner patterns. Japan dominates EUV resists.

nodes.label: Ajinomoto Fine-Techno
nodes.noAlt: Ajinomoto (the MSG company) supplies nearly all Build-up Film used in high-end chip substrates.
nodes.workaround: Sekisui and Taiyo Ink are qualifying alternatives; glass-core substrates are the long-term route around it.
nodes.desc: Turned a by-product of seasoning chemistry into the insulating film inside every AI chip package.

nodes.label: Nittobo glass cloth
nodes.noAlt: Nittobo makes most of the low-expansion 'T-glass' fibre cloth used in high-end substrate cores.
nodes.workaround: Capacity expansions in Japan and Taiwan; slow to qualify.
nodes.desc: Woven glass fibre that keeps big substrates from warping when they heat up.

nodes.label: Wacker Burghausen & Hemlock
nodes.desc: Make electronic-grade polysilicon at 'eleven nines' purity: 99.999999999% silicon.

nodes.label: GE Vernova Greenville
nodes.desc: Builds heavy-duty gas turbines; order book stretches years out because of data centers.

nodes.label: Vertiv plants
nodes.desc: Power and thermal gear for AI halls, co-designed with Nvidia reference designs.

nodes.label: Hitachi Energy transformer works
nodes.desc: Largest transformer maker; multi-billion-dollar expansion driven by data-center demand.

nodes.label: Tesla Fremont & Austin robot lines
nodes.desc: Pilot lines for Optimus actuators and hands.

nodes.label: EssilorLuxottica
nodes.desc: Makes the frames and lenses for Ray-Ban Meta; Meta took a minority stake in 2025.

nodes.label: Electronic-grade polysilicon
nodes.desc: Silicon purified to 11N (one stray atom per 100 billion) via the Siemens trichlorosilane process.

nodes.label: High-purity quartz crucibles
nodes.desc: The quartz bowls that hold molten silicon while ingots are pulled. The purest quartz comes from one place in North Carolina.

nodes.label: EUV photoresist
nodes.desc: Chemically amplified resists, and newer metal-oxide (tin-based) resists for finer lines.

nodes.label: Neon & excimer gases
nodes.desc: Neon carries the ArF/KrF lasers in DUV scanners; about half once came from Ukrainian purifiers fed by Russian steel mills.

nodes.label: Helium
nodes.desc: Cools wafers and purges tools. Comes out of natural gas fields; there is no substitute in many steps.

nodes.label: Fluorine chemicals (HF, NF3, WF6)
nodes.desc: Etch, clean and deposit. Hydrofluoric acid starts from fluorspar, mostly mined in China.

nodes.label: Copper (electroplating & cable)
nodes.desc: Wires every chip (up to ~15 metal layers), every cable and every busbar. A 1 GW site uses thousands of tonnes.

nodes.label: Hafnium oxide precursors
nodes.desc: Hafnium is the 'high-k' insulator under every transistor gate since 2007. It is a by-product of refining nuclear-grade zirconium.

nodes.label: Cobalt & ruthenium liners
nodes.desc: Thin metal liners and contacts in the smallest wires, where copper alone would fail.

nodes.label: Tungsten
nodes.desc: Fills the vertical contacts between transistors and the first metal layer.

nodes.label: Tantalum
nodes.desc: Barrier layers that stop copper from leaking into silicon; comes from coltan ore.

nodes.label: Tin (solder & EUV fuel)
nodes.desc: Micro-bumps join chips to packages; and molten tin droplets are the EUV light source.

nodes.label: Gallium
nodes.desc: In GaN power transistors for rack power and in laser compounds.

nodes.label: Germanium
nodes.desc: In silicon-germanium for photodetectors and fast transistors, and in fibre-optic glass.

nodes.label: Indium phosphide
nodes.desc: The semiconductor that makes the lasers in optical transceivers. Indium is a by-product of zinc refining.

nodes.label: ABF resin & glass cloth
nodes.desc: Epoxy-based build-up film plus woven glass fibre.

nodes.label: Gold & silver
nodes.desc: Contact plating, bond finishes and silver-loaded solders.

nodes.label: Grain-oriented electrical steel
nodes.desc: Special steel whose crystals line up to cut transformer losses; Cleveland-Cliffs is the only US producer.

nodes.label: Nickel superalloys
nodes.desc: Single-crystal turbine blades that survive gas hotter than their own melting point.

nodes.label: NdFeB magnets
nodes.desc: The strongest permanent magnets, inside every robot motor and cooling pump.

nodes.label: Ultrapure water
nodes.desc: A big fab uses tens of thousands of tonnes a day, cleaned until it barely conducts electricity.

nodes.label: Natural gas
nodes.desc: The fastest way to power a new AI campus in the US today, via turbines and engines.

nodes.label: Enriched uranium

teardowns.name: Nvidia GB200 NVL72
teardowns.tagline: The 1.4-tonne rack that acts like one giant GPU.
teardowns.why: Training a frontier model means doing roughly 10^26 multiplications. The NVL72 was the first rack where 72 GPUs share memory over NVLink fast enough to behave as one processor, which is why it became the unit every 2025–26 data center was designed around.

ladder.name: The rack
ladder.see: A 48U cabinet, liquid hoses in and out the back, ~2,000 kg on the floor with its cooling manifold.
ladder.made: Steel and aluminium frame, copper busbar, 18 compute trays, 9 switch trays, power shelves.

ladder.name: Compute tray
ladder.see: A 1U drawer: two Grace Blackwell 'superchips' (4 GPUs + 2 CPUs) under copper cold plates.
ladder.made: Printed circuit board, cold plates, quick-disconnect couplings, BlueField DPUs, ConnectX NICs.

ladder.name: B200 package
ladder.see: Two GPU dies and eight HBM3E stacks on a silicon interposer, on an organic substrate the size of a coaster.
ladder.made: CoWoS-L: dies + local silicon bridges + ABF substrate with ~20 copper layers.

ladder.name: One GPU die
ladder.see: About 800 mm², the largest area a scanner can print in one shot (the 'reticle limit').
ladder.made: ~104 billion transistors on TSMC 4NP, wired by ~15 copper layers.

ladder.name: A Tensor Core cluster
ladder.see: One of 144+ streaming multiprocessors (SMs), each with Tensor Cores that do matrix multiplies in FP4/FP8.

ladder.name: Standard cells
ladder.see: Rows of logic gates (NAND, flip-flops), each a few hundred nanometres wide.
ladder.made: Transistors connected by the first metal layers.
ladder.by: EDA tools from Synopsys and Cadence

ladder.name: A FinFET transistor
ladder.see: A silicon 'fin' wrapped by a gate on three sides. Gate pitch ~50 nm. On/off switch for current.
ladder.made: Silicon fin, hafnium-oxide insulator, metal gate (TiN, TiAl), tungsten contacts, cobalt/copper wires.

ladder.name: Gate oxide
ladder.see: The insulator between gate and channel is ~1.5 nm thick: a handful of atomic layers.
ladder.made: Hafnium dioxide (HfO₂) grown one atomic layer at a time.

ladder.name: Silicon atoms
ladder.see: The channel is a crystal lattice; neighbouring silicon atoms are 0.235 nm apart. Doping adds boron or phosphorus atoms to control conduction.
ladder.made: Si (14), with dopants B (5), P (15), As (33).
ladder.by: Ingot grown from Spruce Pine quartz crucibles

howWorks: A prompt arrives as numbers (tokens). The Grace CPU stages it into GPU memory.
Model weights sit in HBM3E stacks next to each GPU die; 8 TB/s per GPU of bandwidth feeds the cores.
Thousands of Tensor Cores multiply weight matrices by activations in 4-bit or 8-bit floating point, trillions of times a second.
A model too big for one GPU is split across all 72. NVLink switch trays let every GPU swap partial results at 1.8 TB/s.
~1,000+ W per GPU flows into copper cold plates, warm coolant goes to a CDU, then outside to dry coolers or chillers.
Results return through ConnectX/BlueField network cards to the next rack or the user.
howMade: Quartz is smelted to metallurgical silicon, then purified to 11N polysilicon (Wacker, Hemlock).
A seed crystal pulls a 300 mm single-crystal ingot from melt in a quartz crucible; it is sliced and polished (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO).
~80+ mask layers at TSMC: EUV and DUV lithography, etch, deposition, implant, repeated for ~3 months.
Wafers are probed; good dies cut out. Each B200 needs two good reticle-size dies.
SK hynix thins DRAM dies, drills TSVs, stacks 12 high into HBM3E.
GPU dies and HBM are bonded beside each other on silicon bridges and an ABF substrate.
Packages go onto boards with Grace CPUs, cold plates and NICs.
Trays, NVLink spine, power shelves and manifolds are assembled and stress-tested for days before shipping.
elements: Wiring, cold plates, NVLink cables, busbar
money: Nvidia data center revenue, one quarter
Cost of a 1 GW GB200-class campus

teardowns.name: Nvidia Vera Rubin
teardowns.tagline: Shipping since August 2026: HBM4, 3 nm, and an 88-core CPU.
teardowns.why: Each Nvidia generation since 2016 has been 'one year, one architecture'. Rubin roughly triples inference throughput per GPU versus Blackwell Ultra, which is what lets labs serve bigger reasoning models at lower cost per answer.

ladder.name: NVL144 rack
ladder.see: Same Oberon-style rack footprint as GB200, now with 72 Rubin packages (144 GPU dies) and Vera CPUs.
ladder.made: Liquid-cooled trays, NVLink 6 switch trays, 800 V DC power path in newer designs.

ladder.name: Rubin package
ladder.see: Two reticle-size compute dies plus I/O chiplets, surrounded by eight HBM4 stacks.
ladder.made: CoWoS-L on a larger interposer; bigger ABF substrate.

ladder.name: HBM4 stack
ladder.see: 12–16 DRAM layers on a logic base die with a 2,048-bit interface: twice as many wires as HBM3E.
ladder.made: DRAM on 1b/1c-nm class nodes; base die from TSMC (for SK hynix).
ladder.by: SK hynix (majority for Rubin per analysts), Samsung, Micron

ladder.name: Rubin compute die
ladder.see: ~800 mm² of 3 nm logic.
ladder.made: FinFET transistors at ~48 nm gate pitch, 15+ metal layers.

ladder.name: 3 nm FinFET
ladder.see: TSMC's last FinFET node before nanosheets.
ladder.made: Si fins, HfO₂, TiN/TiAl gates, W/Co contacts, Cu/Ru wires.

ladder.name: Atoms
ladder.see: The same silicon lattice as every chip since the 1960s, now with a channel only a few dozen atoms across.
ladder.made: Si, Hf, O, Ti, N, W, Co, Cu, Ru.

howWorks: Modern models 'think' by generating thousands of hidden tokens. Rubin is tuned for this long-decode workload.
Decoding is memory-bound: every new token re-reads the weights. 22 TB/s bandwidth is the headline number for a reason.
Doubles GPU-to-GPU bandwidth so huge mixture-of-experts models can route tokens to experts on other GPUs.
Handles orchestration, KV-cache offload and tool calls next to the GPUs, linked by NVLink-C2C.
howMade: TSMC N3 wafers in Tainan, ~3+ months in the fab.
SK hynix front-end in Icheon/Cheongju, logic base die from TSMC, stacked in Korea.
ODM assembly in Taiwan, Mexico and Texas.

teardowns.name: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM)
teardowns.tagline: A skyscraper of memory chips, drilled through with copper.
facts: Up to 16 dies, up to 64 GB, 2,048-bit bus
teardowns.why: AI is limited less by how fast chips can multiply than by how fast they can fetch numbers. HBM puts memory millimetres from the GPU with thousands of parallel wires. Every AI accelerator, Nvidia or not, depends on these three companies.

ladder.name: The stack
ladder.see: A black rectangle ~11 × 11 mm, about 0.7 mm tall, sitting next to the GPU.
ladder.made: DRAM dies + base die + molded underfill.

ladder.name: A cross-section
ladder.see: Up to 16 dies, each ground to ~30 µm, glued by microbumps or (from HBM4E) direct copper hybrid bonds.
ladder.made: Silicon, copper pillars, tin-silver solder, non-conductive film.

ladder.name: Through-silicon via
ladder.see: A copper-filled hole drilled straight through each die, ~5 µm wide, carrying signals up the stack.
ladder.made: Deep reactive-ion etch, liner, barrier (Ta/TaN), copper fill.

ladder.name: DRAM cell array
ladder.see: Billions of 1-transistor/1-capacitor cells. Each stores one bit as a tiny charge.
ladder.made: Buried word-line transistor plus a tall capacitor.

ladder.name: The capacitor
ladder.see: A pillar dozens of times taller than wide, coated in a high-k dielectric.
ladder.made: Zirconium oxide / hafnium oxide dielectric, TiN electrodes.

ladder.name: One bit
ladder.see: A few femtocoulombs: on the order of thousands of electrons. It leaks away, so every cell is refreshed every ~32–64 ms.

howWorks: A DDR5 chip has a 64-bit bus. An HBM4 stack has 2,048 bits, so it moves far more per clock at lower power.
The stack sits on the same interposer as the GPU; signals travel millimetres, not centimetres.
DRAM forgets: capacitors leak, so the controller re-writes every row constantly.
howMade: Front-end DRAM fabs in Icheon, Pyeongtaek, Hiroshima, Taichung, using EUV on the latest nodes.
For HBM4, a logic die (TSMC for SK hynix; Samsung's own foundry for Samsung).
Drill vias, back-grind wafers to ~30–50 µm on carriers.
Dies stacked one by one with thermo-compression bonding (MR-MUF at SK hynix).
Known-good stacks shipped to TSMC for CoWoS.
money: Several times the price per bit
sources: Silicon Analysts: HBM4 market share race

teardowns.name: CoWoS advanced packaging
teardowns.tagline: Where a GPU becomes a GPU: dies and memory married on silicon.
teardowns.why: Chips got too big for one die and memory had to move closer. CoWoS lets several dies and HBM stacks talk at terabytes per second. From 2023 to 2025 it was the single tightest bottleneck: Nvidia could get wafers but not enough packaging.

ladder.name: Finished package
ladder.see: A substrate the size of a coaster with a metal lid.
ladder.made: ABF substrate, interposer, dies, HBM, lid.

ladder.name: Interposer / bridges
ladder.see: CoWoS-L uses small 'local silicon interconnect' bridges inside an organic layer instead of one huge silicon slab.
ladder.made: Silicon bridges with fine copper wiring, redistribution layers.

ladder.name: Substrate layers
ladder.see: ~20 layers of copper traces in ABF film around a glass-fibre core.

ladder.name: Microbumps
ladder.see: Tens of thousands of solder bumps ~25–40 µm apart join each die to the interposer.
ladder.made: Copper pillars capped with tin-silver solder.

ladder.name: Redistribution wires
ladder.see: Copper lines ~1–2 µm wide fan signals between GPU and HBM.

ladder.name: Copper atoms
ladder.see: Copper's lattice spacing ~0.256 nm; electromigration at high current slowly pushes these atoms along the wire.

howWorks: Dies and memory sit next to each other with ~thousands of short wires instead of a few long ones.
Only the areas that need ultra-dense wires get silicon bridges; the rest is cheaper organic material.
The substrate spreads connections to a few thousand balls that solder to the server board.
howMade: TSMC makes silicon bridges and builds redistribution layers on a carrier wafer.
Known-good GPU dies and HBM stacks are bonded onto the wafer.
The assembly is cut and attached to the ABF substrate, lidded and tested.
money: Tens of thousands of dollars per wafer
sources: Tom's Hardware: TSMC fab expansion roadmap (Jun 2026)

teardowns.name: ASML EUV lithography scanner
teardowns.tagline: A machine that makes light by blowing up tin, 50,000 times a second.
teardowns.why: To print features of a few dozen nanometres you need light with a wavelength near that size. Only ASML, after ~20 years and help from Intel, Samsung and TSMC, got 13.5 nm 'extreme ultraviolet' light working in production. Every leading AI chip passes through these machines dozens of times.

ladder.name: The machine
ladder.see: About the size of a bus, inside a cleanroom, connected to a separate laser room below.
ladder.made: Light source, illuminator, reticle stage, projection optics, wafer stages.

ladder.name: Drive laser
ladder.see: A CO₂ laser amplifier of 20+ kW, built from thousands of parts.

ladder.name: Mirrors
ladder.see: EUV is absorbed by air and glass, so everything is in vacuum and every optic is a mirror.
ladder.made: ~40–50 alternating molybdenum and silicon layers, each a few nanometres thick, reflecting ~70% per mirror.

ladder.name: Tin droplet
ladder.see: Molten tin droplets ~25 µm wide fall through a vessel; a pre-pulse flattens each, then the main pulse turns it into plasma at ~200,000 °C that emits 13.5 nm light.

ladder.name: The light
ladder.see: A 13.5 nm photon carries ~92 eV, enough to ionise atoms in the photoresist.

ladder.name: Photoresist molecules
ladder.see: Resist molecules react where light lands, writing the pattern; stochastic 'shot noise' of few photons is now a key limit.

howWorks: Laser hits tin droplet, tin becomes plasma, plasma glows at 13.5 nm.
A collector mirror gathers light; the illuminator shapes it.
The pattern sits on a reflective mask (reticle).
Projection mirrors shrink the image 4× (8× in one direction for High-NA) onto the wafer.
Stages moving at several g's scan each field, aligned to better than a nanometre, ~150+ wafers per hour.
howMade: Zeiss polishes and coats mirrors over many months.
Cymer builds the tin vessel; Trumpf the laser.
Assembled and tested in Veldhoven, then disassembled and flown to the fab.
Months of re-assembly and qualification in the customer cleanroom.
elements: Hydrogen gas cleans tin off optics

teardowns.name: A 2 nm transistor
teardowns.tagline: From beach sand to a switch a few dozen atoms wide.
teardowns.why: Every AI calculation is a transistor turning on or off. Making them smaller cuts energy per operation; that is the whole reason we can afford AI at all.

ladder.name: 300 mm wafer
ladder.see: A mirror-polished silicon disc holding a few dozen big AI dies or hundreds of phone chips.

ladder.name: A die
ladder.see: One chip, after dicing.

ladder.name: Metal stack
ladder.see: Copper wires get wider going up; the bottom ones are ~10–12 nm wide. A16 adds power wires on the back side.

ladder.name: Nanosheet transistor
ladder.see: Three or four horizontal silicon ribbons stacked like a sandwich, each wrapped on all four sides by the gate.
ladder.made: Si sheets, SiGe sacrificial layers (removed), HfO₂, work-function metals.

ladder.name: One nanosheet
ladder.see: ~5 nm thick: roughly 20 silicon atoms.

ladder.name: Atoms
ladder.see: At this scale, a few misplaced dopant atoms change how a transistor behaves; variability is the enemy.
ladder.made: Si, Ge, Hf, O, Ti, N, B, P.

howWorks: A small voltage on the gate pulls electrons into the channel (on) or pushes them away (off).
Wrapping the gate on all sides stops leakage that plagued FinFETs at small sizes.
Billions of these switches combine into adders and multipliers that do matrix math.
howMade: Czochralski pulling in a Spruce Pine quartz crucible.
Epitaxy grows alternating silicon and silicon-germanium.
Fins and gates printed with EUV, often with multiple exposures.
SiGe is etched away selectively, leaving floating silicon ribbons.
HfO₂ and metal deposited atom by atom around each sheet (ALD).
Contacts and 15+ copper layers; inspected at every step.

teardowns.name: Google TPU (Ironwood → TPU 8)
teardowns.tagline: Google's own chip, wired together with mirrors that steer light.
teardowns.why: The TPU is the most proven alternative to Nvidia. Because Google designs the chip, network, compiler and model together, it can tune the whole stack, and in 2025–26 it began selling that capacity at huge scale to rivals such as Anthropic.

ladder.name: A pod
ladder.see: Thousands of chips across many racks, wired in a 3D torus.
ladder.made: Racks, optical circuit switches, liquid cooling.

ladder.name: Optical circuit switch
ladder.see: A box of tiny MEMS mirrors that re-aim laser beams to rewire the pod in seconds, routing around failed chips.

ladder.name: TPU tray
ladder.see: Four chips per board under cold plates.

ladder.name: TPU chip
ladder.see: Compute dies plus HBM stacks on CoWoS.
ladder.by: Broadcom physical design; MediaTek on some variants

ladder.name: Matrix multiply unit (MXU)
ladder.see: A systolic array: a grid of multiply-accumulate cells where data pulses through like blood through a heart.

ladder.name: Transistors and atoms
ladder.see: Same silicon lattice as every other chip.

howWorks: Weights load once; activations flow across the grid, each cell multiplying and passing the sum on, so data is reused without trips to memory.
Dedicated units for embedding lookups used in recommendation and some model layers.
Chips talk directly over Inter-Chip Interconnect; optical switches reconfigure the topology for each job.
Google's compiler turns model code into TPU instructions; this software stack is the real moat.
howMade: Google architects; Broadcom turns it into a manufacturable chip.
Assembled by ODMs, installed in Google data centers.
sources: Anthropic: SpaceX compute deal and partners

teardowns.name: A gigawatt AI campus (Stargate Abilene)
teardowns.tagline: A city's worth of electricity, turned into tokens.
teardowns.why: The model is only as big as the building. A 1 GW campus uses as much power as ~750,000 US homes, and most of the hard problems (permits, turbines, transformers, water, labour) are not about chips at all.

ladder.name: The campus
ladder.see: Hundreds of acres of West Texas: halls, substations, gas generation, cooling yards.

ladder.name: A data hall
ladder.see: One building ~100+ MW, rows of racks on slab floors.
ladder.made: Pre-fab electrical rooms, cooling loops, cable trays.

ladder.name: Substation & transformers
ladder.see: Grid voltage (hundreds of kV) stepped down to medium voltage, then low voltage at the rack.
ladder.made: Grain-oriented steel cores, copper windings, oil.
ladder.by: Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova

ladder.name: Gas turbine
ladder.see: On-site generation to supplement the grid.

ladder.name: One rack
ladder.see: ~130 kW per GB200 rack: as much as ~100 homes.

ladder.name: Coolant
ladder.see: Water-glycol at ~25–45 °C flowing through copper cold plates and back to dry coolers.

ladder.name: Electrons and molecules
ladder.see: Every watt becomes heat carried away by water molecules.

howWorks: Grid + on-site generation → substations → transformers → busways → rack power shelves (54 V or 800 V DC).
Racks join into a cluster through three networks: NVLink (in rack), InfiniBand/Ethernet back-end (between racks), front-end (to the internet).
~100% of the electricity becomes heat; closed-loop liquid cooling uses little water once filled.
With 100,000+ GPUs, something fails every few hours; training jobs checkpoint constantly to survive.
howMade: Find land with a power path (grid interconnect, gas line) and permits.
Order transformers and turbines years ahead.
Concrete and steel, with prefab electrical rooms.
Racks arrive pre-integrated and burned-in from ODMs.
sources: Epoch AI: where the Stargate sites stand

teardowns.name: A large language model
teardowns.maker: OpenAI · Anthropic · Google DeepMind · Meta · others
teardowns.tagline: Trillions of numbers, learned from text, that predict the next word.
teardowns.why: This is what all the steel, silicon and gas is for. A model is a file of numbers (weights). It is 'made' by running the hardware above for months, and 'works' by running it again for every word you read.

ladder.name: The model
ladder.see: A file of ~10¹² numbers, a few terabytes in 8-bit form.

ladder.name: Transformer layers
ladder.see: ~100 identical blocks stacked; each refines the meaning of every token.

ladder.name: Attention
ladder.see: Each token looks back at every earlier token and decides which ones matter.

ladder.name: A token's vector
ladder.see: Each word-piece is a list of ~10,000 numbers that encodes its meaning in context.

ladder.name: One weight
ladder.see: A single number in 4–16 bits, stored as charge in HBM and as voltage in SRAM.

ladder.name: Electrons
ladder.see: In the end, an AI's knowledge is a pattern of electrons in memory cells, and its thinking is electrons switching transistors.

howWorks: Your text is split into tokens (word-pieces) and turned into vectors.
In each layer, attention mixes information between tokens.
The last layer outputs a probability for every possible next token; one is sampled.
The new token is appended and the process repeats. Reasoning models do this thousands of times privately before answering.
Agents call search, code and other tools between tokens.
howMade: Web text, books, code, licensed data, synthetic data, and human-written examples.
Predict the next token across trillions of tokens on 100,000+ accelerators for months.
Supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human and AI feedback, and RL on verifiable tasks (code, math).
Capability, safety and misuse testing; frontier models now go through government and third-party evaluation.
Weights copied to inference clusters worldwide; served by batching many users per GPU.
elements: Every transistor that trains and runs it
Natural gas burned to power it
Nuclear fuel powering some of it
sources: Vaswani et al., 'Attention Is All You Need' (2017)
Kaplan et al., 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models' (2020)

teardowns.name: 1.6T optical transceiver
teardowns.tagline: Turns electricity into laser light so racks can talk.
facts: Several modules in a large cluster
Indium phosphide EML or silicon photonics
teardowns.why: A 100,000-GPU cluster needs millions of optical links. Optics are now one of the largest costs and power draws in the network, and indium phosphide lasers are a quiet bottleneck.

ladder.name: The module
ladder.see: A metal plug (OSFP) the size of a pack of gum, plugged into a switch.

ladder.name: DSP chip
ladder.see: Cleans up 200 Gb/s signals; often made by Broadcom or Marvell at TSMC.

ladder.name: Laser chip
ladder.see: A sliver of indium phosphide that emits infrared light at ~1,310 nm.

ladder.name: Quantum wells
ladder.see: Layers a few nanometres thick where electrons and holes recombine to make photons.

ladder.name: InP lattice
ladder.see: Indium and phosphorus atoms alternating in a zinc-blende crystal (lattice constant ~0.587 nm).
ladder.by: Indium from zinc smelters like Korea Zinc

howWorks: The DSP turns parallel data into fast serial streams.
A laser's light is switched on and off (or in four levels, PAM4) billions of times a second.
Light travels through glass fibre with almost no loss.
A germanium or InGaAs photodiode converts light back to current.
howMade: Lasers, lenses, fibre and DSP aligned to micron precision.
money: Tens of billions $ per year, growing with each cluster

teardowns.name: Humanoid robot (Tesla Optimus)
teardowns.why: Robots move AI from screens into the physical world, and add a new set of chokepoints: rare-earth magnets, precision screws and gears, and batteries.

ladder.name: The robot
ladder.see: A humanoid frame with cameras in the head.
ladder.made: Aluminium, steel, plastics, battery pack in the torso.

ladder.name: An actuator
ladder.see: Motor + gearbox or roller screw + sensors + controller in one unit.
ladder.made: Motor, planetary roller screw or harmonic drive, encoder.

ladder.name: Motor
ladder.see: Copper windings around a rotor of permanent magnets.

ladder.name: Magnet grains
ladder.see: Micron-sized grains of Nd₂Fe₁₄B; dysprosium at the grain edges keeps them strong when hot.
ladder.made: Nd, Pr, Fe, B, Dy, Tb.

ladder.name: Atoms
ladder.see: Neodymium's 4f electrons produce the strong magnetic moment.

howWorks: Cameras feed a vision network (like FSD).
An end-to-end policy outputs joint targets many times a second.
Each actuator's controller drives its motor to the commanded position and force.
Data from teleoperation, video and simulation trains the policy on the Cortex cluster.

teardowns.name: Ray-Ban Meta glasses
teardowns.tagline: An AI that sees what you see, in a 50-gram frame.
teardowns.why: Glasses are the most likely 'next phone' for AI: always there, hands-free, with a camera at eye level. They show how tiny the physical slice of AI can be when most of the thinking happens in a distant data center.

ladder.name: The glasses
ladder.see: Wayfarer frames hiding cameras, five microphones, speakers and a battery in the arms.

ladder.name: AR1 chip
ladder.see: A Qualcomm processor with an NPU that wakes on 'Hey Meta' and handles photos.

ladder.name: Waveguide (Display)
ladder.see: A lens with microscopic structures that bend a tiny projector's light into your eye.

ladder.name: Camera pixel
ladder.see: ~1 µm pixels in a CMOS sensor turn photons into electrons.

ladder.name: Atoms
ladder.see: Silicon, lithium (battery), gallium (LEDs).

howWorks: Microphones and the NPU detect the wake word.
Camera takes a photo when you ask about what you see.
Via your phone, the request goes to Meta's data centers (e.g. Prometheus) where Meta AI answers.
Answer plays through open-ear speakers or appears on the Display lens.

teardowns.name: A frontier training run
teardowns.tagline: 100,000 chips doing one multiplication problem for three months.
facts: A hardware fault every few hours
teardowns.why: Training is where most of the capital goes. Getting 100,000 chips to act as one machine is a systems problem as much as a research one: networks, memory, failures and power swings decide how much of the theoretical compute turns into a better model.

ladder.name: The cluster
ladder.see: One job spread across ~100,000 accelerators in one or several buildings, sometimes several campuses linked by dedicated fibre (Microsoft Fairwater, Google multi-site TPU).
ladder.made: Data parallelism across groups of replicas; gradients averaged every step.
ladder.by: Cluster schedulers, NCCL / JAX / Neuron collectives

ladder.name: A pipeline stage group
ladder.see: The model's layers are cut into stages; micro-batches flow through like an assembly line (pipeline parallelism).
ladder.made: 1F1B / interleaved schedules to hide 'bubbles' of idle time.

ladder.name: One scale-up domain
ladder.see: Tensor and expert parallelism live inside the fast domain (NVL72, TPU slice, Trn UltraServer) because they talk every layer.
ladder.made: NVLink / ICI / NeuronLink all-to-all for mixture-of-experts routing.

ladder.name: One accelerator
ladder.see: Holds a shard of weights, optimizer state (often 2–3× the weights in FP32) and activations; recomputes some activations to save memory.
ladder.made: HBM capacity is usually the binding limit.

ladder.name: One step's math
ladder.see: Each token costs ~6 FLOPs per parameter in training (2 forward, 4 backward). Multiply by tokens and you get the run's total compute.
ladder.made: Matrix multiplies in BF16/FP8 with FP32 accumulation.

ladder.name: One tensor-core instruction
ladder.see: A small matrix multiply-accumulate (e.g. 16×8×16) issued by a warp; everything above is billions of these.

howWorks: Trillions of filtered, deduplicated tokens stream from storage, tokenised and shuffled.
Each micro-batch runs through every layer, producing a loss: how wrong the next-token guesses were.
Gradients flow back through the layers (2× the forward compute).
Gradients are averaged across data-parallel replicas over the scale-out network; overlapping this with compute is the core trick.
AdamW-style update of every weight, sharded across chips (ZeRO / FSDP).
State is saved every few minutes to hours so a failed chip costs minutes, not days.
After pre-training, RL on verifiable tasks runs many inference rollouts per update, blurring training and inference hardware.

glossary: Token
A word-piece. Models read and write tokens; ~0.75 English words each.
Parameter
One learned number (weight) in a model. Frontier models have hundreds of billions to trillions.
MoE (mixture of experts)
A model where each token only uses a few 'expert' sub-networks, so a 1T-parameter model may compute with only ~30B active parameters per token.
Pre-training
Learning to predict the next token over trillions of tokens. The most compute-hungry phase.
Post-training / RL
Fine-tuning after pre-training: supervised examples, RLHF, and reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks like code and math.
Inference
Running a trained model to answer requests. Now the majority of AI compute spend.
KV cache
Saved attention keys and values for every past token, so the model doesn't recompute them. Long contexts make it huge and push demand for HBM.
Prefill vs decode
Prefill reads the whole prompt at once (compute-bound); decode writes one token at a time (memory-bandwidth-bound). Rubin CPX targets prefill.
FLOP / PFLOPS / EF
Floating-point operation. PFLOPS = 10¹⁵ per second; an exaflop (EF) is 10¹⁸.
FP8 / FP4 / NVFP4
8- and 4-bit number formats. Fewer bits = more math per watt; NVFP4 adds block scaling so 4-bit stays accurate.
Dense vs sparse FLOPS
Vendors often quote 2:4 structured-sparsity numbers, which are 2× dense. This atlas uses dense where it can.
MFU
Model FLOPs Utilization: the share of a chip's peak math a training job actually achieves. 35–50% is good at scale.
6ND rule
Training compute ≈ 6 × parameters × training tokens (in FLOPs) for a dense transformer.
HBM
High-Bandwidth Memory: DRAM dies stacked with through-silicon vias and placed beside the GPU.
TSV
Through-silicon via: a copper-filled hole through a thinned die that carries signals vertically.
CoWoS
TSMC's Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate packaging that puts logic and HBM side by side on silicon.
SoIC / hybrid bonding
Stacking dies face-to-face with direct copper-to-copper bonds, no solder bumps.
Reticle limit
The largest area a scanner prints in one exposure, ~858 mm² (26 × 33 mm). High-NA EUV halves it.
EUV / High-NA EUV
13.5 nm-wavelength lithography from ASML. High-NA (0.55) prints finer lines but with a half-size field.
GAA / nanosheet
Gate-all-around transistor: stacked silicon ribbons wrapped by the gate on four sides. Replaces FinFET at 2 nm.
Backside power
Moving power wires to the back of the wafer (TSMC A16, Intel PowerVia) to free the front for signals.
Scale-up vs scale-out
Scale-up links chips into one memory domain (NVLink, ICI); scale-out links domains into a cluster (InfiniBand, Ethernet).
NVLink / NVSwitch
Nvidia's GPU-to-GPU link and switch that make 72 GPUs behave like one.
UALink / UEC
Open industry alternatives to NVLink (UALink) and to InfiniBand (Ultra Ethernet).
OCS
Optical circuit switch: MEMS mirrors that reroute light between TPU racks without converting to electrons.
CPO
Co-packaged optics: lasers and photonics on the switch package, cutting transceiver power.
Rail-optimized fabric
A network where GPU #k in every server connects to the same switch 'rail', reducing hops for collective operations.
All-reduce
The collective operation that averages gradients across all GPUs every step; network bandwidth caps it.
PUE
Power usage effectiveness: total facility power ÷ IT power. Liquid-cooled AI halls reach ~1.1–1.2.
Liquid cooling (DLC)
Direct-to-chip liquid cooling through cold plates; required above ~40–50 kW per rack.
800 V DC
Higher-voltage rack power that Nvidia is moving to for ~1 MW racks, reducing copper.
Behind-the-meter
Power generated on-site (gas turbines, fuel cells) without waiting for a grid connection.
Interconnection queue
The wait to connect to the grid; years in many US regions and the real limit on AI build-out.
Neocloud
GPU-specialist clouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe.
ASIC / XPU
Custom accelerator designed for one company (TPU, Trainium, Maia, MTIA), often with Broadcom or Marvell.
Chokepoint
A step with one or two suppliers worldwide and no quick substitute.

W.role: Contacts between transistors and the first wiring layer.

Co.role: Contacts and liners in the finest wires; superalloys; batteries.

Ru.role: Liners for the narrowest wires; capping layer on EUV mirrors.

Ta.role: Barrier that stops copper diffusing into silicon; capacitors.

Ti.role: Titanium nitride gate metals and electrodes.

N.role: Nitrides (TiN, TaN, GaN), and nitrogen purge gas everywhere in the fab.

O.role: Oxides: HfO₂ gates, SiO₂ insulators; water.

H.role: Hydrogen cleans tin off EUV mirrors; ultrapure water; natural gas fuel.

He.role: Cools wafers, purges tools, laser gas; no substitute in many steps.

Ne.top: By-product of steel-mill air separation; Ukraine was ~50% pre-2022

Ar.role: Sputtering and inert atmospheres; ArF laser gas.

F.role: Etch gases (CF₄, NF₃), hydrofluoric acid, WF₆, photoresist.

Sn.role: Solder micro-bumps; molten tin droplets are the EUV light source; metal-oxide resists.

Au.role: Contact finishes, bond pads, MEMS mirrors.

Ga.role: GaN power transistors for rack power; InGaAs lasers; LEDs.

Ge.role: SiGe layers for nanosheet transistors and photodetectors; fibre glass.

In.role: Indium phosphide lasers in optical transceivers; ITO; thermal interface.

As.role: Dopant; gallium arsenide and InGaAs in optics.

Al.role: Work-function tuning in gates; heat sinks, frames, busways.

C.role: Epoxies, photoresists, ABF film, natural gas, CO₂ laser gas.

S.role: Photoresist acid generators; sulfuric acid cleans.

Fe.role: Steel racks and buildings; grain-oriented transformer steel; NdFeB magnets.

Nd.role: Permanent magnets in robot motors, pumps, fans, speakers.

Li.role: Batteries in robots, glasses, backup power (BESS) at data centers.

U.role: Nuclear fuel for plants signed to power AI campuses.
